biggest_gap.what: This piece's headline artifact is a three-arm experiment showing the shipped panner at r = 0.9999 and the rule it replaced at r = −0.5207 on the same fixture, and it concludes `detector_goes_red = true`. The −0.5207 is a property of that fixture, not of the rule. Under the legacy rule a blow the player lands is positioned at the attacker, so dx = dz = 0 and pan = sin(atan2(0,0) − playerYaw) = sin(−playerYaw): the target's position is NEVER READ, and the correlation with the target's true bearing is therefore whatever the fixture's player-yaw history happens to make it. Sweeping the fixture on the shipped code at HEAD 5c4c5b0, the same broken rule scores r = −0.0759 (orbit anchored to player facing), +0.7768 (orbit anchored to world — within 0.03 of the bar), +0.6034 (stationary target, player free to turn), null (still target), and +1.0000 with 100 impacts, 99 distinct pan values and a 70° bearing spread on 'stationary enemy, player turning on the spot'. On that last fixture the BROKEN rule PASSES M6 outright and the shipped `detector_goes_red` predicate reports green. That fixture is not exotic: it is a player circling a standing enemy, which is what M6's own method text ('correlate audioLog.pan against the enemy's bearing from the player') invites a critic to build. The invariant that does discriminate is already in every log row and is not in the pass condition: distance_m_max is 0.0000 on all five legacy arms and 1.13–1.45 m on all five shipped arms.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The shipped panner is correct — that is not in dispute and the fix was a real one. What is broken is the thing that certifies it. A check that reports green on the exact anti-pattern the piece exists to have removed is worse than no check, because the next critic will run M6 the obvious way, get r ≈ 1.0, and bank a regression as a pass. RI-AUD02 S6 explicitly delegates its own non-self-report backstop to this measurement ('the camera-orbit pan measurement, which cannot be self-reported wrongly'), so two items rest on it. And the shipped sabotage switch — setAudioPanSource('attacker'), the mechanism that exists so a build cannot run the defect quietly — is only as good as the predicate reading it. AGENT-PROTOCOL rule 4: a probe that cannot fail is worse than no probe, and this one cannot fail on a fixture a reasonable person would choose.

remedy.action: Make M6's pass condition test the property that is actually invariant, and make the fixture sweep part of the check rather than a single hand-picked orbit. Concretely: (1) add `distance_m` to the P4 pass condition — a player-landed impact must report a non-zero distance to the listener, and the legacy rule cannot satisfy that on any fixture; (2) run P4 over at least the 'stationary target, player turning' fixture in addition to the orbit, and require the shipped rule to pass ALL of them and the sabotaged rule to fail ALL of them, rather than requiring one arm to go red; (3) fold tools/audio/critic-m6-fixture-sweep.mjs (or its logic) into tools/audio/impact-browser.mjs so the sweep runs where the real WebAudio panner does. The tool already exits 3 when it finds a fixture on which the broken rule passes, so it is its own regression test.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/audio/critic-m6-fixture-sweep.mjs exits 0 with finding 'LEGACY_NEVER_PASSES' — i.e. no fixture in the sweep passes the acceptance criterion under panSource='attacker' — while the shipped rule passes every fixture in the sweep; and impact-browser.mjs P4 reports the same across at least two fixture geometries.

why_the_biggest_gap_is_not_the_mass_defe: It is the larger defect and it is recorded as this verdict's only triggered hard fail (RI-WPN05/M5b: 63 clips whose weapon socket moves over a metre in one 60 Hz frame, worst 2.5869 m), which is why the piece's status is FAIL. It is not named as biggest_gap because it already has a full diagnosis, a named successor and a written handover — and the successor, W1-MASS, reports `state: complete` while the census at HEAD is unchanged on every row. Naming it again would add no information the next builder does not have. The M6 gap is this piece's own, is unowned, and is the kind that causes a FALSE PASS rather than a visible failure.

secondary_observations.what: MASS, RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE IT IS THE HARD FAIL. At HEAD 5c4c5b0, after W1-MASS reported complete: 63 clips over §E.2's 1.00 m socket hard fail (worst whp_hist_bindings/r2 2.5869 m; eight of the worst ten are cgs_drowned_reaper, the baseline heavy greatsword, at 1.26–1.52 m per frame — 76–91 m/s of socket travel); tip speed over 1.25× the tier band on 41.42% of 606 clips (the builder measured 43.4% at 0b2d6ef, so it has moved 2 points, not been fixed); arc nonconforming 3.96% against a 2% bar; follow-through under band 7.59% with 14 clips dead. The root cause the builder found is correct and worth keeping: game/src/combat/swing.js `calibrateYawGain` solves for the DECLARED arc over the ACTIVE WINDOW ALONE, and its objective contains no tip-speed, no continuity and no recovery term, so the one thing that is solved is the one thing that passes.

gap_closure.measured_value: Perturbing the victim's material on a loaded copy changes the resolved impact class, the audio recipe and the gain; zeroing the §A hitstop table on a loaded copy takes 28 of 35 attacker cells from their declared frame counts to 0. ar3.note: Not sterile. The lore fact (a root-warden is plant, a golem is stone) is a combat answer and now an AUDIBLE one — but only two-thirds of the way: §A gives the material twelve classes and no stone or metal among them, so mat_stone and mat_metal both route to C02 while correctly carrying their own material on the event. The builder declared that limit honestly rather than hiding it, and it belongs in a wave-2 §A extension.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-WPN05 §A publishes a 5×7 grid and M1 diffs against it at ±0 f@60, but game/src/combat/impact.js honours a per-slot `hitstop_f` override and cites §A as the licence for it. §A contains no such licence. Is a per-weapon impact row legal (and if so, does M1 diff the CLASS table or the EFFECTIVE table), or is the override a defect? Four weapons and 102 slots turn on the answer, and three of them ship the same override table across two weight tiers.

RI-WPN05 §F defines the Impact Legibility Score over the observable triple (attacker_hitstop, camera_shake_peak, knockback_m), and §C hands the shake row to RI-CAM06. RI-CAM06's shake has no world-side caller. Does ILS get computed from the impact RECORD's shake_deg (in which case the 'observable' in §F means 'recorded'), or is ILS unmeasurable until the camera actually shakes on a landed blow? This verdict scored it unmeasurable; the ruling should be written down.

corpus_extended.what: M6 is specified as 'correlate audioLog.pan against the enemy's bearing from the player in the trace frame. Pearson r over >=20 events', pass at r >= 0.8, hard fail 'no panner at all'. Demonstrated here: a build that positions EVERY voice at the listener - the exact one-sword-at-your-own-feet failure the item's How-we-lose section is about - scores r = 1.0000 over 100 events on an ordinary fixture (stationary enemy, player turning), and scores anywhere from -0.0759 to +0.7768 on four others. The correlation is a property of the fixture because the broken rule never reads the target's position at all. PROPOSED AMENDMENT, not applied by this critic: M6 gains a second, fixture-independent condition - for an impact whose victim is not the listener, audioLog.distance_m must equal the true world distance from the listener to the victim to within a stated tolerance and must be non-zero - and M6's method requires the correlation to be taken over at least two fixture geometries, one with the target moving and one with the player turning.
corpus_extended.why_the_item_and_not_the_build: The shipped panner is correct on every fixture tried. What fails is the check, and the check is the item's, so the correction belongs in the item rather than in a builder's remedy. CORPUS-CONTRACT: a constructed threshold that cannot separate the failure it names is a bar defect.
corpus_extended.note: Not applied by this critic: RI-AUD01 is judged by this verdict, and a critic editing the bar it is scoring against in the same round is exactly the move CORPUS-CONTRACT forbids. Filed for the corpus owner with the reproduction in hand.

self_audit.self_audit_note: TWO FALSE, both for the same reason and both reported rather than worked around. `ran_every_assigned_method` is false: RI-AUD01 M2 and M8 have no instrument in the tree (recorded as unmeasurable, scored 0 fail-closed, filed as corpus_debt and as steps 2 and 3 of path_to_ten); RI-WPN05 M4 and M6 were not run (M4 unrun, M6 unmeasurable because one of its three observables has no world-side consumer); RI-CAM06's other seven checks are out of remit. `blind_done_where_required` is false: all three of RI-AUD01, RI-WPN05 and RI-CAM06 are `blind_pair: yes`, and no blind pack was run. RI-AUD01's pack tool is an absence-reporter; RI-WPN05's and RI-CAM06's packs need a browser, and AGENT-PROTOCOL rule 21's ~8-browser ceiling was exceeded (12 at start, 24 during the M6 work, loadavg 13.52). Because no blind ran, `critic.saw_builder_notes_before_blind` is recorded true conservatively and there was no blind for it to contaminate. Escalation ladder, in order: (1) re-ran the piece's own headline instruments at HEAD and reproduced them; (2) perturbed the tables the piece says are consumed and confirmed the world moved — hitstop and material both pass; (3) deleted the fix and confirmed the old number returns, which is where the ranged-override finding came from; (4) stopped trusting the reported number and asked whether the FIXTURE, not the build, produced it — which is where the biggest gap is; (5) ran the aggregation (boot-check, check-data, motion-census, audio-sync, audio-budget) rather than only the standalone probes.
